# `sesam rm` stops tracking a secret: it records a secret.remove entry, drops the
# entry from the config, prunes the sealed object and deletes the plaintext.
# Plaintext with unsealed changes is refused unless --force is given.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Track two secrets.
exec sesam add keep.txt --group dev
exec sesam add drop.txt --group dev
exists .sesam/objects/drop.txt.sesam
exec sesam ls
stdout 'drop.txt'

# Remove one: audit records secret.remove, it leaves the listing and config, and
# the sealed object is pruned.
exec sesam rm drop.txt
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"secret.remove"'
exec sesam ls
! stdout 'drop.txt'
stdout 'keep.txt'
! exists .sesam/objects/drop.txt.sesam
! grep 'drop.txt' sesam.yml
exec sesam verify

! exists drop.txt

# Unsealed edits are the only copy: refused, and nothing changes.
cp edited.txt keep.txt
! exec sesam rm keep.txt
stderr 'refusing to remove 1 unsealed secret'
stderr 'keep.txt'
exists keep.txt
exec sesam ls
stdout 'keep.txt'

# --force deletes them anyway.
exec sesam rm keep.txt --force
! exists keep.txt
exec sesam verify

# A directory deletes only the secrets' plaintext, never files sesam does not
# manage.
exec sesam add conf/db.env --group dev
exec sesam rm conf
! exists conf/db.env
exists conf/app.yaml
exec sesam verify

# A secret added without sealing has no other copy either.
exec sesam add unsealed.txt --group dev --no-seal
! exec sesam rm unsealed.txt
stderr 'unsealed.txt'
exists unsealed.txt

# Several paths at once remove all of them.
exec sesam add one.txt two.txt --group dev
exec sesam rm one.txt two.txt
exec sesam ls
! stdout 'one.txt'
! stdout 'two.txt'

-- edited.txt --
keep me, edited
-- unsealed.txt --
never sealed
-- one.txt --
1
-- two.txt --
2
-- keep.txt --
keep me
-- drop.txt --
drop me
-- conf/db.env --
db secret
-- conf/app.yaml --
not a secret
